Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — folks on our platform security and legal teams reviewed Redwood's private deployment options and we have a couple of open items before we can proceed to procurement:

1) Key custody model: our default preference is a custodian-only (customer-held) model where Redwood's operators never possess plaintext keys. We need confirmation of technical controls (HSM split, no key material on host, attestations).

2) Subprocessor audit window: we need a written commitment that customers will get at least 30 days notice before onboarding any operator subprocessor with access to telemetry; additionally, we ask for quarterly attestation summaries.

3) Escrow: we see references in the template to potential escrow for recovery purposes. We prefer alternatives to keystore escrow unless dual-control escrow is negotiated.

I attached our annotated DPA (Medica_DPA_v1.pdf). Could you confirm Redwood's stance on the three items above and suggest redlines?

Best,

Marta — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the annotated DPA. I did a quick pass with the Solutions and Security teams and here are the practical positions we can commit to up-front: 

- Key custody: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) in Private deployments. We do not require customer key escrow for standard installs. Where customer requests recoverability, we can discuss a dual-control escrow (Redwood + customer KMS holder) as a paid addendum — but this is not the default.

- Operator access/telemetry: Our standard operator telemetry for Private is limited to service health, GPU process metrics, and anonymized error traces. We do not collect request payloads or decrypted model inputs. We can provide the exact telemetry schema and an attestation of non-collection of plaintext data.

- Subprocessor notice: We can accept a 30-day notice for any operator-level subprocessor that would have access to operator-facing telemetry, and we can provide quarterly attestation for operational changes.

I'll put legal on the thread to produce redlines for the DPA and propose language for the subprocessor notice clause and operator telemetry schema. Attached is a first-pass redline for the BYOK section (Redline_BYOK_terms.pdf).

Next steps: Kimberly from Legal will follow up with formal redlines. If those look OK we can move to DocuSign and proposed installation windows. Any constraints on timing from your side?

Hi all — quick technical confirmation from Security/Infrastructure: 

1) BYOK enforcement model we recommend: customer provides KMS credentials that grant Redwood ephemeral wrapping key rights only. Redwood never persists plaintext key material. Keys are bound to HSM-backed envelopes; the runtime requests unwrapping operations through a signed, short-lived token. We can support customer HSMs (if reachable) or customer-managed cloud KMS with VPC peering.

2) Operator telemetry: we will limit operator-facing telemetry to the following fields: service_health_status, node_gpu_utilization (aggregated), agent_error_code (no stack with request payloads), session_start/stop timestamps (no user identifiers). Retention: 90 days by default, configurable down to 30 days at customer's request. We will include this schema in the DPA as an appendix.

3) Subprocessor notice & attestation: 30 days notice is acceptable for operator subprocessors with potential access to runtime telemetry; we will provide a quarterly attestation report listing subprocessors, their roles, and whether they had any access to operator telemetry. For high-sensitivity customers (e.g., regulated PHI workloads), we can move to a 60-day notice + pre-approval workflow.

4) Escrow: we will not accept unilateral escrow of customer key material without dual-control. If Medica requires key-recovery, propose a dual-signature escrow held by an independent custodian (we can recommend vendors) and documented release criteria.

5) Breakglass / emergency access: we can support a documented breakglass procedure (audit trail + immediate customer notification) but access requires both a documented approval workflow and cryptographic approval from the customer's KMS.

Ben / Kimberly — I've sketched precise telemetry JSON schema and the BYOK enforcement API (see internal Drive link). Marta — linking the DocuSign envelope here: https://app.docusign.com/documents/EXAMPLE-DSIGN-ID-78234. If the redlines look OK we'll push the envelope and calendar a staging window (approx 3 business days after signed).

Cheers,
